title: The Kiva Method for Inclusive Decision-Making
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article revives an old decision-making structure drawn from the Hopi nation, in which concentric circles of leaders discuss an issue in sequence, from most to least experienced, while outer circles only observe. After each circle deliberates and the senior group states a tentative decision, the process rotates so less experienced voices can respond, ultimately returning to the most senior group to revisit and possibly revise its conclusion. The author presents the Kiva Method as a structured way to gather broad organizational input without the chaos of too many voices competing at once, producing decisions with deeper shared understanding and stronger buy-in.
points: The Kiva Method, drawn from Hopi decision-making tradition, structures debate in concentric circles by experience level.
Only the innermost circle speaks at a time while outer circles observe and listen.
The process cycles through circles from most to least senior, then returns to the center for a final decision.
It can involve up to 36 leaders across three circles without descending into chaotic cross-talk.
The result is a decision with deeper shared understanding and stronger organizational buy-in.
quotes: The tribal elders of the Hopi nation knew a thing or two about inclusive decision-making.
The so-called Kiva Method, drawn from the structures in which the decisions were made and devised generations ago, allows minor voices to influence more experienced views.
The most inner circle begins to debate and discuss the issue in question without any input from those in the two outer circles.
With each new discussion at the center, the outer rings only listen and learn, refraining from offering any input.
The power of this method revolves around its ability to create an inclusive discussion without having too many voices and viewpoints on the table at the same time.
By tapping into the collective wisdom of the organization’s leaders, perhaps no other method is equal to it.
